# CLORE.AI

> CLORE.AI is the world's largest decentralized GPU cloud marketplace. Rent GPU servers for AI training, ML inference, rendering, and compute workloads. Pay per minute in Bitcoin, CLORE tokens, USDT, or USDC with no minimum commitment.

## What is CLORE.AI?

CLORE.AI is a peer-to-peer marketplace connecting GPU owners with users who need compute power. Hosts list their servers, renters choose from thousands of GPUs at competitive prices. All workloads run inside Docker containers for isolation and portability. The platform supports both on-demand rentals (fixed price) and spot market (auction-style bidding for lower prices).

Founded in 2022, CLORE.AI has grown to become one of the largest decentralized GPU cloud platforms.

## Network Stats

- 12,000+ GPUs available for rent
- 3,000+ servers across 50+ countries
- Per-minute billing with no minimum commitment
- Average GPU utilization rate above 60%

## Available GPU Models

The marketplace offers a wide range of NVIDIA GPUs:
- Consumer: RTX 4090, RTX 4080, RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX 3070
- Professional: A100 80GB, A100 40GB, A6000, A5000, A4000, L40S
- Data Center: H100, A100 SXM, V100

Pricing varies by GPU model, VRAM, and market demand. The MFP (Maximum Fair Price) algorithm ensures fair pricing across the marketplace.

## Payment Methods

- Bitcoin (BTC)
- CLORE token (ERC-20 on Ethereum)
- USDT (Tether)
- USDC (USD Coin)
- Per-minute billing, pay only for what you use
- No upfront costs or long-term contracts

## Key Features

### For Renters
- **On-Demand Rentals**: Rent GPU servers at fixed prices set by hosts
- **Spot Market**: Bid on GPUs at auction rates for lower prices
- **Docker-Based**: All workloads run in Docker containers — anything that runs in Docker runs on CLORE.AI
- **SSH Access**: Full root SSH access to rented servers
- **Jupyter Notebooks**: Pre-configured environments for AI/ML workflows
- **Multi-GPU Support**: Rent servers with multiple GPUs for distributed training
- **API Access**: Programmatic server management via REST API

### For Hosts (GPU Owners)
- **Passive Income**: List your GPUs and earn per-minute when rented
- **Auto-Mining**: When not rented, GPUs automatically mine cryptocurrency
- **Marketplace Rewards**: Additional CLORE token rewards for hosting
- **Flexible Pricing**: Set your own prices or use MFP algorithm

### Proof of Holding (PoH)
- Lock CLORE tokens in your wallet for benefits
- Fee discounts up to 50% on marketplace transactions
- Priority access to high-demand GPUs
- Additional staking rewards (current APY ~16%)
- No lockup period — withdraw anytime with no penalties

## CLORE Token

- **Type**: ERC-20 token on Ethereum
- **Max Supply**: 1,300,000,000 CLORE
- **Utility**: Payment for GPU rentals, PoH staking, DAO governance, marketplace fee discounts
- **Exchanges**: HTX, MEXC, Gate.io, BingX
- **Contract**: 0xe60201989b8628f43dc0605f585a72bcf1f1e977

## Use Cases

- **AI Model Training**: Train LLMs, diffusion models, and other deep learning models on multi-GPU setups
- **ML Inference**: Deploy models for inference at scale
- **3D Rendering**: GPU-accelerated rendering for Blender, Octane, and other tools
- **Scientific Computing**: Run simulations, molecular dynamics, and research workloads
- **Data Processing**: Large-scale data pipelines and ETL workloads
- **Fine-Tuning**: Fine-tune open-source LLMs (LLaMA, Mistral, etc.) on your own data

## Governance (DAO)

CLORE.AI operates a decentralized autonomous organization where token holders can:
- Submit and vote on protocol proposals
- Influence platform development direction
- Participate in treasury allocation decisions

## Key Differentiators

- Largest decentralized GPU network (12,000+ GPUs)
- Crypto-native payments: BTC, CLORE, USDT, USDC
- Per-minute billing with no minimum commitment
- Spot market with auction-style bidding for lowest prices
- PoH staking rewards for token holders (~16% APY)
- Auto-mining for hosts when GPUs are idle
- Fully decentralized with DAO governance

## Landing Pages by GPU

Each NVIDIA GPU model on the marketplace has two dedicated landing pages — one for users who want to rent the GPU, and one for hosts who want to list/monetize their hardware. URLs follow the pattern `/rent-{slug}.html` and `/host-{slug}.html`.

### Rent (use the GPU)

#### Consumer

- [Rent RTX 3070](https://clore.ai/rent-3070.html): 8 GB GDDR6, entry-level inference and SD 1.5
- [Rent RTX 3080](https://clore.ai/rent-3080.html): 10 GB GDDR6X, mid-tier inference, SDXL 1024²
- [Rent RTX 3090](https://clore.ai/rent-3090.html): 24 GB GDDR6X, budget 24 GB workhorse for QLoRA and SDXL
- [Rent RTX 4070](https://clore.ai/rent-4070.html): 12 GB GDDR6X Ada, low-power SDXL/ComfyUI workhorse
- [Rent RTX 4070 Ti](https://clore.ai/rent-4070-ti.html): 12 GB GDDR6X Ada, sweet spot between 4070 and 4080
- [Rent RTX 4080](https://clore.ai/rent-4080.html): 16 GB GDDR6X, Ada-class inference and 7B fine-tuning
- [Rent RTX 4090](https://clore.ai/rent-4090.html): 24 GB GDDR6X, most-rented consumer card
